subject: Request: Structured SLO reserve & exit payment for Redwood platform
messages:
From: Bryan Kline <bk@acme-industries.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: lisa.m@acme-industries.com
Date: Sat, 21 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Structured exit payment & SLO fund - Redwood platform

Monica,

Thanks for taking this. As part of Acme's procurement review we need to lock down stronger remedies than service credits for platform availability and latency because we run customer-facing workflows that are revenue-critical. High-level ask below — happy to run through by phone this week.

What we're asking for (initial proposal):
- Uptime SLO: 99.95% monthly for the Redwood-hosted endpoint (us-west region)
- Latency SLO: P95 < 200ms for standard generation requests
- If an SLO is missed for 3 consecutive months, Acme may elect to terminate for convenience with a fixed exit payment equal to 3 months of committed spend (liquidated damages), OR Redwood pre-funds an SLO reserve/escrow equal to two months' committed spend to be used to compensate Acme for verified outages.
- We want objective measurement hooks (per-route dashboards or signed trace logs) and the right to trigger a forensic audit if counts disagree.

The alternative we can consider is a staged cure approach with a pre-funded SLO reserve, but procurement needs the ability to recover predictable sums or exit without protracted litigation.

We're planning to finalize procurement terms by EOD Friday (2027-08-27). Please confirm whether Redwood can support either: (a) capped exit payment (fixed number of months) or (b) pre-funded SLO reserve held in escrow. Also send any standard counter language if you have one.

Attaching a short SLO summary for Acme's legal and procurement team.

Thanks,
Bryan Kline
Senior Procurement Manager
Acme Industries
Attachments: SLO-proposal-Acme-v1.pdf
---

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Bryan Kline <bk@acme-industries.com>
Cc: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Structured exit payment & SLO fund - Redwood platform

Bryan — thanks for the clear note and the SLO summary. I looped in Rohan (legal) and Priyom (contracts) so we can give a coordinated response. We appreciate Acme's need for predictability; A couple of quick points up front:

- Redwood's standard remedy for availability/latency is service credits tied to verified SLO misses; we prefer credits because they preserve the commercial relationship and avoid double recovery.
- That said, for enterprise commitments we are open to a capped fee-at-risk structure or an escrowed SLO reserve as a trade — with limits and objective verification steps.

To be concrete, can you confirm: 1) committed monthly/annual spend baseline, 2) whether this applies to all routes or only a defined set (e.g., user-facing generation API), and 3) whether Acme will accept Redwood-run verification with agreed dashboards/logging before any escrow payout/termination right triggers?

I've attached our suggested term-sheet template for these scenarios (Acme-MA-Redwood-term-sheet.xlsx) — it shows two paths: escrowed SLO reserve (prefund 25–50% of one month) or capped exit payment (1–3 months) with a required multi-step cure process. Rohan, Priyom — can you weigh in on the redline approach and whether legal would accept an escrow vs. buyout schedule?

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-min sync tomorrow if that helps.

Best,
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1-415-555-0123
Attachments: Acme-MA-Redwood-term-sheet.xlsx
---

From: Bryan Kline <bk@acme-industries.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Lisa Moreno <lisa.m@acme-industries.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Structured exit payment & SLO fund - Redwood platform

Monica,

Quick answers:
- Committed baseline: ~$540k/mo (we plan to commit 6 nodes initially, onboarding ramp in Q4)
- Applies to core generation route (/v1/generate) and embeddings for customer search (we can provide a small set of route IDs)
- We are willing to accept Redwood-run verification provided logs/dashboards are exportable and there's a narrow window for Acme to request an independent audit (once per incident).

Procurement note: our legal team is risk-averse — the escrow approach is preferred if Redwood can: (a) pre-fund a reserve equal to two months' committed spend, (b) permit Acme to draw from the reserve for verified outages after the cure process, or (c) allow termination after two validated, non-cured months with a partial return of any unused escrow.

If Redwood cannot pre-fund, the next-best is a capped exit payment of 3 months' spend with a clear definition of sustained breach. We are open to negotiating the exact cure windows but need a firm cap on the customer's downside exposure.

Let's aim for a brief sync Thursday to align redlines so both legal teams have something to review by Monday.

-Bryan
---

From: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>
To: Bryan Kline <bk@acme-industries.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Aug 2027 10:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Structured exit payment & SLO fund - Redwood platform

Bryan — appreciate the clarity and the spend figures. Quick read from legal on the major points and a proposed counter that balances Acme's need for predictability with Redwood's operational risk:

- Escrowed reserve: Redwood cannot pre-fund third-party escrow for customer-specific failures. We can, however, agree to an SLO Reserve mechanism where Acme prepays an agreed amount (25% of one-month committed spend by default) into a dedicated, single-purpose account managed by a neutral trustee. The reserve is refundable pro rata for periods without SLO breaches and is available for customer compensation for verified outages after the escalation/cure process.

- Cure & remediation: before any draw or termination, parties must follow a three-step process: (1) detection & notification with 5 business-day investigation window, (2) remediation plan and 30 calendar-day cure period, (3) independent verification if material disagreement persists. For prolonged or repeated failures (defined as 2 out of 3 months breaching the same SLO), Acme may elect termination for convenience with a buyout schedule equal to 2 months' committed spend, reduced by any draws from the SLO Reserve.

- Measurement and audit: Redwood will provide per-route dashboards and signed daily summaries for the affected routes; Acme may request a forensic audit once per rolling 12 months at its cost unless Redwood materially disputes the results — in which case costs are split if the auditor finds the breach.

- Cap and limitation: total exit liability capped at 6 months' committed spend over the term across all breaches; Redwood will not agree to uncapped liquidated damages.

In short: we can offer a funded SLO Reserve (customer-funded, trustee-managed), a defined cure flow, a capped buyout option, and limited audit rights. I've attached our counter redlines (redwood-counter-redlines.docx) with clause text.

If that direction is acceptable in principle, Monica and I can jump into a call with your procurement and legal to finalize precise wording.

Rohan Mehta
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-counter-redlines.docx
---

From: Bryan Kline <bk@acme-industries.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Lisa Moreno <lisa.m@acme-industries.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Aug 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Structured exit payment & SLO fund - Redwood platform

Rohan / Monica — this reads like a reasonable path. A couple of clarifying requests before we escalate to our CPO:

1) Can we make the trustee entity options explicit (we prefer an industry-standard escrow provider; please propose three names) and confirm timing for establishing the reserve (we need deposit within 30 days of contract effective date).
2) We need the buyout schedule in the term sheet to show math: if we prepay two months into the reserve and later terminate after 2 validated months of breach, what is the net payout to Acme? Your note about reducing buyout by draws makes sense — please put an example in the term sheet so procurement can sign off.
3) For independent verification: we accept 'one free audit per 12 months' but we need Redwood to preserve logs for 12 months and export them within 5 business days of request.

If you send a clean term sheet with the trustee options and the worked example, I will route to our CPO and legal this afternoon. Looking forward to the short call to finalize.

Thanks,
Bryan Kline
Senior Procurement Manager, Acme Industries
Phone: +1-206-555-4455
